# Project Plan

## Start-Up Phase

<!--
Covering the planning phase, this section should provide a relatively
detailed plan of how work will start on the project. This section is
important because projects need to get up and running quickly.


 - [ ] Setting up collaboration platform inc. code for contributors etc.
 - [ ] License decisions
 - [ ] Reporting framework
-->

The first milestone (M1) will begin in December 2026, after the grant agreement.
I will pin versions of ten evaluation packages, define their editing workflows,
and record baseline diagnostics and response times. I will reproduce the
analysis problems, starting with existing cases from `future`, and document the
setup for comparison with the final results.

Initial extraction checks in September 2026 found the required fields for every
exported function in glue, withr, R6, and cli. For magrittr, coverage was 16 of
42 functions, largely because primitive aliases lack formal arguments. The
checks also found S3 methods incorrectly listed as exports. The metadata pilot
will use glue, withr, R6, and cli, along with tinytable to test a package
outside the existing bundle. I will also use magrittr to test incomplete
indexes. I will fix the S3 export errors during M1, before publication.

During M1, I will identify the overlapping code, missing APIs, and tests needed
to consolidate the readers in r-documentation-rs. I will also test extraction of
deprecation declarations and define the supported cases before M4. If full
consolidation exceeds the available hours, I will retain the necessary parts of
Arity's extractor and defer the remaining consolidation work.

Before M4, five pilot packages must pass the metadata quality criteria below. A
prototype using Arity's existing client must provide signatures and help without
local installation for packages both inside and outside the existing bundle. If
the pilot fails to meet these requirements within budget, I will agree on a
revised scope for the metadata milestones with the ISC.

## Technical Delivery

<!--
Covering the actual delivery of the project this section should
provide at least a high-level description of the implementation.

Including target dates is really important as you need to be committed
and the ISC need to have a means of tracking delivery
-->

I plan to spend about 25 hours per month on the project, completing the 125
hours by April 30, 2027. The target dates reflect the estimated effort for each
milestone.

  | Milestone                        | Target date       | Deliverables                                                                                                                | Hours   | Cost (USD) |
  | :--------                        | :----------       | :-----------                                                                                                                | ----:   | ---------: |
  | M1: Baseline and pilot           | January 7, 2027   | Baseline, metadata prototype, consolidation plan, quality checks, regression cases                                          |      30 |      2,400 |
  | M2: Documentation analysis       | January 19, 2027  | Correct handling of shared and inherited roxygen documentation and detection of undocumented parameters                     |      10 |        800 |
  | M3: Navigation and safe renaming | February 6, 2027  | Consistent references and call hierarchy for quoted names, safe renaming including infix calls                              |      15 |      1,200 |
  | M4: Reusable package metadata    | February 28, 2027 | Indexes for at least 100 CRAN packages meeting the quality criteria, documented schema, extraction pipeline, weekly updates |      20 |      1,600 |
  | M5: Package metadata in Arity    | March 25, 2027    | Completion, hover, signature help, deprecation diagnostics, bulk prefetch, shared offline cache for editor and CLI          |      20 |      1,600 |
  | M6: Validation and release       | April 30, 2027    | Workflow validation, annotated comparison, guides, release, report, maintenance instructions                                |      30 |      2,400 |
  | **Total**                        |                   |                                                                                                                             | **125** | **10,000** |

M2 and M3 can each be funded independently of the other implementation
milestones. M4 delivers a reusable dataset and publishing pipeline for other R
tools. M5 depends on M4.

The estimates include regression tests and two hours in each of M2--M5 for
unexpected work, totaling eight hours. If the grant agreement is delayed, I will
agree on revised milestone dates with the ISC before work begins.

## Other Aspects

<!--
How will you ensure that your work is available to the widest number
of people? Please specify the open-source or creative commons license(s)
you will use, how you will host your code so that others can contribute,
and how you will publicize your work. We encourage you to plan content
to be shared quarterly on the R Consortium blog.

 - [ ] Announcement post
 - [ ] Delivery blog post
 - [ ] Social media
 - [ ] UseR!
 - [ ] ISC meetings
-->

Code and tests will use Arity's MIT license. Evaluation sources and examples
will retain applicable notices. I will publish the schema, code for the
publishing pipeline, documentation, and results, along with instructions for
rebuilding or mirroring the dataset.

I will invite package authors and tooling developers to try a prerelease and
write R Consortium blog posts announcing the project and sharing results,
examples, and limitations.

## Budget & Funding Plan

<!--
Note that the maximum grant is $10k USD. The proposal should be in USD.

Outline the milestones for development and how much funding will be
required for each stage (as payments will be tied to project milestone
completion). This also helps the ISC in the event of partial funding.
Each milestone should specify the work to be done and the
expected outcomes, providing enough detail for the ISC to understand
the scope of the project work and assess the likelihood of success.

We expect that most of the budget will be allocated
for labor costs. We do not cover indirect costs. The ISC grants cannot
cover such things as travel, lodging, food, journal publication fees,
or personal hardware. Cloud services may be covered if they are specific
to the project and the project period. The ISC reserves the right to vet
how funds are used for each project separately. If in doubt, please reach
out to us.
-->

I intend to receive the grant personally. The requested USD 10,000 will fund 125
hours of my time at USD 80 per hour. The budget assumes no other funding or
contributors.

With partial funding, the ISC could select implementation milestones according
to their value to the R community and the dependencies described above. I would
adjust the scope and budgets of M1 and M6 to cover the selected work. For
example, funding M4 without M5 would deliver the reusable metadata and pipeline,
with extraction checks and maintenance instructions. Funding M2 or M3 would
focus the baseline, workflow validation, and release on those improvements.
Before accepting partial funding, I would agree with the ISC on the selected
milestones, hours, funding, dates, and corresponding completion criteria.
